scenes.line1: Ever had one project break another?
scenes.line2: How do you stop dependency chaos?
scenes.say: Ever had one Python project break another? How do you stop dependency chaos for good?

scenes.label: Isolation
scenes.sub: Virtual environments keep each project's packages separate.
scenes.say: Virtual environments keep each project's packages completely separate from the rest of your system.

rows.b: Switch your shell to use it
Add packages just for this project

scenes.say: Here's how it works: First, create an environment. Next, activate it so your shell uses the right Python. Then, install packages just for this project.

scenes.title: Creating and using venv
scenes.say: You make a new environment, activate it, and install your dependencies. This keeps your global Python clean.

scenes.question: What's a common mistake with venv?
scenes.right: Always activate your environment first, or you risk polluting your system Python and breaking other projects.
scenes.say: A common mistake? Installing everything globally. Always activate your environment first, or you risk polluting your system Python and breaking other projects.
